mainTopic: Why the שופר is blown twice, רבי יצחק's teachings on judgment and the רגל, and the three books opened on ראש השנה.
overview: The גמרא finishes explaining why we blow the שופר both sitting and standing: it confuses the שטן. רבי יצחק then gives a long series of teachings. A year with no שופר at its start meets trouble at its end. A year that starts poor ends rich. A person is judged only by what he is doing right now. Three things bring up a person's sins, and four things (צדקה, crying out, a new name, better deeds) can tear up a bad decree. Some add moving to a new place, but רבי יצחק credits ארץ ישראל in the story of אברם. He also teaches that one must greet his רבי on the רגל and must be טהור for the רגל, which a ברייתא supports. The גמרא then returns to ראש השנה: three books are opened, for צדיקים, רשעים and בינוניים, with two פסוקים as sources. A ברייתא of בית שמאי describes three groups at the future יום הדין, and its account of the בינוניים continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Blowing twice confuses the שטן
steps.stepSummary: The question about blowing the שופר while standing ends, and the answer is that it confuses the שטן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do we blow a תקיעה and a תרועה again while standing? To confuse the שטן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes asking why we blow the שופר a second time, during the standing עמידה. It answers that we do this to confuse the שטן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first blowing was already done while people were sitting, so the second one looks extra. The answer is that the extra blowing has a purpose: it throws off the שטן, who wants to accuse the Jewish people in judgment.

keyTerms.meaning: they blow a תקיעה (a long straight blast)
while they are standing, during the עמידה

steps.whyThisMatters: This is where the custom of blowing the שופר both before מוסף and during מוסף comes from.

phrases.english: and then sound a tekia and a terua again while they are standing?
In order to confuse the Satan.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּדֵי לְעַרְבֵּב הַשָּׂטָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a question begun earlier on the daf and gives its answer.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The second blowing is done to confuse the שטן.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why is the שופר blown a second time while standing?

steps.title: A year without שופר at its start
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק teaches that a year in which the שופר is not blown at its beginning will have trouble at its end.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: any year in which they do not blow the שופר at its start will have trouble at its end.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק gives a new teaching linked to the שופר. If the שופר is not blown at the start of the year, the year will end badly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word מריעין plays on two meanings: 'blowing a תרועה' and 'bringing harm' (from the word רע, bad). If the year missed its תרועה at the beginning, it gets a different kind of 'תרועה', meaning trouble, at its end.
steps.confusionAlert: Here מריעין does not mean blowing the שופר. It is a play on words meaning 'harm comes to it'.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yitzḥak said:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל שָׁנָה שֶׁאֵין תּוֹקְעִין לָהּ בִּתְחִלָּתָהּ
phrases.english: Any year during which the shofar was not sounded at its beginning
will suffer misfortune at its end.
phrases.notes: Wordplay: מריעין can mean 'blow a תרועה' or 'bring harm'.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק כׇּל שָׁנָה שֶׁאֵין תּוֹקְעִין לָהּ בִּתְחִלָּתָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the idea from step 1 that the שופר confuses the שטן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A year without שופר blowing at its start meets misfortune at its end.

steps.title: The reason: the שטן was not confused
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why a year with no שופר ends badly: the שטן was never confused.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? Because the שטן was not confused.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי יצחק's rule is true. It answers that without the שופר the שטן was not confused, so he could accuse freely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ties step 2 straight back to step 1. The שופר protects us by confusing the שטן. With no שופר, that protection is missing and his accusations can bring punishment.
steps.whatToRemember: The שופר works like a shield against the שטן's accusations. Without it, the year can end in trouble.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
Because Satan was not confused.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּלָא אִיעַרְבַּב שָׂטָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for רבי יצחק's teaching in step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does a year without שופר end badly?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The שטן was not confused, so his accusations worked.

steps.title: A poor beginning leads to a rich ending
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק teaches that a year that starts poor will end rich, learned from how a פסוק is spelled.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: any year that is poor at its beginning will become rich at its end. The פסוק says 'from the beginning of the year', but the word is spelled like 'poverty'. It continues 'until the end', meaning that year will have a good future.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק gives a new teaching about judgment: a year that starts out poor will end rich. He proves it from the spelling and the wording of a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word מראשית (beginning) is spelled without an א, so it can be read as מרשית, from רש (poor). The end of the פסוק, ועד אחרית, is read as a promise that such a year has a good אחרית, a hopeful ending.

keyTerms.meaning: it is written (this is how the word is spelled)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yitzḥak said:
Any year that is poor at its beginning
will be made rich at its end,
for it is stated: "From the beginning of the year"
phrases.notes: דברים 11:12

phrases.english: the word is written "mereishit"
phrases.notes: It is spelled without an א, so it looks like the word for being poor (רש).

phrases.english: "And until the end"
meaning that its end will have a good future.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק כׇּל שָׁנָה שֶׁרָשָׁה בִּתְחִלָּתָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching from the same רבי יצחק, now about a year's fortunes rather than the שופר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A year that begins poor ends rich, learned from the spelling מרשית in דברים 11:12.

steps.title: A person is judged by what he is doing now
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק teaches that a person is judged only by his actions at that moment, learned from ישמעאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: a person is judged only by his deeds at that time, as it says: 'For God heard the voice of the lad where he is.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק teaches that a person is judged by how he is acting right now, not by what he will do later. He brings a פסוק about ישמעאל as proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'באשר הוא שם', 'where he is', mean that God looked at ישמעאל as he was in that moment. Even though bad things would come from him later, his prayer was answered because at that time he was innocent.

keyTerms.meaning: where he is, in his present state

steps.whatToRemember: On יום הדין a person is judged by who he is right now, not by his future.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives hope on ראש השנה: what counts is where a person stands at the moment of judgment.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yitzḥak said:
A man is not judged

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לְפִי מַעֲשָׂיו שֶׁל אוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה
phrases.english: except according to his deeds at that time,
as it is stated:
"For God has heard the voice of the lad
phrases.notes: בראשית 21:17. The lad is ישמעאל.

phrases.english: where he is."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק אֵין דָּנִין אֶת הָאָדָם אֶלָּא לְפִי מַעֲשָׂיו שֶׁל אוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another teaching about judgment in the series from רבי יצחק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person is judged only by his present deeds, learned from 'באשר הוא שם'.

steps.title: Three things that bring up a person's sins
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק lists three behaviors that cause Heaven to examine a person's sins: sitting by a leaning wall, expecting one's prayer to be answered, and handing a case against another person over to Heaven.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יצחק said: Three things bring a person's sins to mind. They are: a leaning wall, expecting one's prayer to be answered, and handing over judgment of one's fellow to Heaven.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק gives a new list of three things that make Heaven take a close look at a person's sins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each item is a situation where a person puts himself up for inspection. Standing by a wall about to fall puts him in danger, so the question becomes whether he deserves to be saved. Counting on his prayer, or asking Heaven to judge someone else, makes Heaven weigh his own record.

keyTerms.meaning: Bring sins to mind, cause them to be examined
A leaning wall that may collapse
Expecting or counting on one's prayer being answered
Handing a case against another person over to Heaven to judge

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yitzchak said:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים מַזְכִּירִין עֲוֹנוֹתָיו שֶׁל אָדָם,
phrases.english: Three things bring a person's sins to mind,
and they are: a leaning wall,
and expecting one's prayer to be answered,
and handing over judgment against one's fellow.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: שְׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים מַזְכִּירִין עֲוֹנוֹתָיו שֶׁל אָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another teaching in the series of statements from רבי יצחק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sitting by a leaning wall, counting on one's prayer, and asking Heaven to judge another all cause one's own sins to be examined.

steps.title: Proof that asking Heaven to judge another brings punishment first
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבין supports the third item: whoever asks Heaven to judge another is punished first, as seen with שרה, who asked God to judge between her and אברהם and died before him.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי אבין said: Anyone who hands over judgment against his fellow is punished first. As it says: 'And שרי said to אברם, My anger is upon you,' and it is written: 'And אברהם came to mourn for שרה and to weep for her.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רבי אבין's teaching to explain and support the third item on רבי יצחק's list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שרה complained to אברהם and asked God to judge between them. Later the תורה tells us that אברהם mourned שרה, which means she died first. רבי אבין reads this as the punishment for calling on Heaven to judge someone else.

keyTerms.meaning: My anger (the wrong done to me) is upon you

phrases.english: For Rabbi Avin said:
Anyone who hands over judgment against his fellow,
he is punished first,
as it is said: "And Sarai said to Abram,
My anger is upon you,"
phrases.notes: בראשית טז:ה. The same פסוק ends with her saying 'let ה׳ judge between me and you.'

phrases.english: and it is written: "And Abraham came to mourn for Sarah and to weep for her."
phrases.notes: בראשית כג:ב. Since he mourned her, she died first.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אָבִין: כָּל הַמּוֹסֵר דִּין עַל חֲבֵירוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up the third item in step 6.
steps.raayaObject: That handing over judgment of another to Heaven brings up one's own sins.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שרה's complaint (בראשית טז:ה) followed by her dying before אברהם (בראשית כג:ב).

steps.title: Four things that tear up a bad decree
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק teaches that four things can tear up a bad decree against a person: צדקה, crying out in prayer, changing one's name, and changing one's deeds.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יצחק said: Four things tear up a person's decree. They are: צדקה, crying out, changing the name, and changing deeds.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק gives a list of four things that can cancel a bad decree. The next step will bring a פסוק for each one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last list was about what brings sins up. This list is the hopeful side: even after a bad judgment is decided, these four actions can tear it up.

keyTerms.meaning: Crying out to ה׳ in prayer
Changing one's deeds for the better

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yitzchak said:

phrases.aramaic: אַרְבָּעָה דְּבָרִים מְקָרְעִין גְּזַר דִּינוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם,
phrases.english: Four things tear up a person's decree,
and they are: charity, crying out,
a change of name, and a change of deeds.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: אַרְבָּעָה דְּבָרִים מְקָרְעִין גְּזַר דִּינוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching of רבי יצחק, the hopeful flip side of step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: צדקה, prayer, changing one's name, and changing one's deeds can tear up a bad decree.

steps.title: A פסוק for each of the four things
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a פסוק for each item: צדקה saves from death, crying out brings rescue, שרה's new name brought a son, and the people of נינוה changed their deeds and were spared.
steps.simpleTranslation: צדקה, as it is written: 'And צדקה saves from death.' Crying out, as it is written: 'They cried to ה׳ in their trouble, and He brought them out of their distress.' Changing the name, as it is written: 'שרי your wife, do not call her name שרי, for שרה is her name,' and it is written: 'And I will bless her, and I will also give you a son from her.' Changing deeds, as it is written: 'And God saw their deeds,' and it is written: 'And God relented from the evil He had said He would do to them, and He did not do it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes through the four items one by one and gives a פסוק that shows each one works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first two פסוקים say it outright. For the last two, the גמרא puts two פסוקים side by side: first the change (a new name, new deeds), then the good result (a son, the punishment cancelled).

keyTerms.meaning: And He relented, changed the plan

phrases.english: Charity, as it is written: "And charity saves from death."
phrases.notes: משלי י:ב

phrases.aramaic: צְעָקָה, דִּכְתִיב: ״וַיִּצְעֲקוּ אֶל ה׳ בַּצַּר לָהֶם
phrases.english: Crying out, as it is written: "They cried to the Lord in their trouble,
and He brought them out of their distress."
phrases.notes: תהלים קז:כח

phrases.english: A change of name, as it is written: "Sarai your wife,
do not call her name Sarai,
for Sarah is her name,"
phrases.notes: בראשית יז:טו

phrases.english: and it is written: "And I will bless her,
and I will also give you a son from her."

phrases.aramaic: שִׁינּוּי מַעֲשֶׂה, דִּכְתִיב: ״וַיַּרְא הָאֱלֹהִים אֶת מַעֲשֵׂיהֶם״,
phrases.english: A change of deeds, as it is written: "And God saw their deeds,"
phrases.notes: יונה ג:י, about the people of נינוה who did תשובה.

phrases.english: and it is written: "And God relented from the evil

phrases.aramaic: אֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּר לַעֲשׂוֹת לָהֶם וְלֹא עָשָׂה״.
phrases.english: that He had said He would do to them, and He did not do it."

steps.triggerLanguage: צְדָקָה, דִּכְתִיב: וּצְדָקָה תַּצִּיל מִמָּוֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for each of the four items in step 8.
steps.raayaObject: That each of the four things can tear up a decree.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משלי י:ב; תהלים קז:כח; בראשית יז:טו-טז; יונה ג:י.

steps.title: Some add a fifth: changing one's place
steps.stepSummary: Some say that changing where you live also tears up a decree, since ה׳ told אברם to leave his land and then promised to make him a great nation.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say: Also changing one's place, as it is written: 'And ה׳ said to אברם, Go out from your land,' and then: 'And I will make you a great nation.'
steps.whatsHappening: A different opinion adds a fifth item to רבי יצחק's list: moving to a new place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof works the same way as the earlier ones: first the change (אברם leaves his land), then the good result (he will become a great nation, even though he had no children).

phrases.english: And some say: also a change of place,
as it is written: "And the Lord said to Abram,
Go out from your land,"
phrases.notes: בראשית יב:א

phrases.english: and afterward: "And I will make you a great nation."
phrases.notes: בראשית יב:ב

steps.triggerLanguage: וְיֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים: אַף שִׁינּוּי מָקוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a fifth item to the list in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Changing one's place can also tear up a decree.

steps.title: Why רבי יצחק does not count changing place
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the other view: אברם was helped by the merit of ארץ ישראל, not by the move itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one? It was the merit of ארץ ישראל that helped him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי יצחק left changing place off his list: he reads the אברם proof differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יצחק agrees that אברם's luck changed after he moved. But he says the reason was where he went, ארץ ישראל and its special merit, not the act of moving. So the proof does not show that any move helps.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one (the opinion that disagrees)
Helped him, was useful to him

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יצחק is not saying moving is harmful. He is saying the אברם story does not prove that a move by itself helps, because ארץ ישראל was the reason.

phrases.english: And the other one?
phrases.notes: That's רבי יצחק, who did not list changing place.

phrases.english: That was the merit of the Land of Israel
that helped him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידַּךְ: הָהוּא זְכוּתָא דְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא דְּאַהַנְיָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns down the proof from step 10 according to רבי יצחק.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof that changing place by itself tears up a decree.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: אברם's success came from the merit of ארץ ישראל, not from moving.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יצחק: four things tear up a decree (צדקה, צעקה, שינוי השם, שינוי מעשה). Some add שינוי מקום, but רבי יצחק credits ארץ ישראל in the אברם story.

steps.title: A person must greet his רבי on the רגל
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק teaches that a person must go greet his teacher on the רגל, learned from the husband of the Shunamite woman, who asked why she was going to the נביא when it was not חודש or שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יצחק said: A person must greet his teacher on the רגל, as it says: 'Why are you going to him today? It is not חודש and not שבת.' This shows that on חודש and שבת she was supposed to go.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק gives a new rule about the יום טוב: a student must go visit his רבי, and he proves it from a story about the נביא אלישע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband asks why she is going on an ordinary day. That suggests that on special days, going to the נביא was expected. The גמרא draws the rule from this hint (מכלל) and applies it to visiting one's רבי on the רגל.

keyTerms.meaning: To go greet one's teacher in person
By inference, from what is implied

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the custom of going to visit one's רבי on יום טוב.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yitzchak said:

phrases.aramaic: חַיָּיב אָדָם לְהַקְבִּיל פְּנֵי רַבּוֹ בָּרֶגֶל,
phrases.english: A person is obligated to greet his teacher on the festival,
as it is said: "Why are you going to him today?
phrases.notes: מלכים ב ד:כג. The Shunamite woman's husband says this when she goes to אלישע.

phrases.english: It is not the New Moon and not Shabbat,"
which implies that on the New Moon and on Shabbat
she was supposed to go.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: חַיָּיב אָדָם לְהַקְבִּיל פְּנֵי רַבּוֹ בָּרֶגֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another teaching of רבי יצחק, this time about the יום טוב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person must go greet his רבי on the רגל, learned by inference from מלכים ב ד:כג.

steps.title: A person must purify himself for the Festival
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק teaches that a person must make himself טהור on the רגל, based on the פסוק ״וּבְנִבְלָתָם לֹא תִגָּעוּ״.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יצחק said: A person is obligated to purify himself on the Festival, as it says: "And their carcasses you shall not touch."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק gives another teaching about the רגל: everyone has to be טהור for it. He brings a פסוק as his source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new idea is that being טהור is required, not just a nice extra, during the רגל. At this point it is not yet clear how the פסוק about a נבלה shows this. The next steps explain it.

keyTerms.meaning: One of the three pilgrimage festivals
The carcass of an animal that was not properly slaughtered

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yitzchak said:
A person is obligated to purify himself
on the Festival,
as it is stated: "And their carcasses you shall not touch."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 11:8

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: חַיָּיב אָדָם לְטַהֵר אֶת עַצְמוֹ בָּרֶגֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second teaching from רבי יצחק about the רגל, following his teaching about visiting one's רבי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every person must make himself טהור for the רגל.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows ordinary Jews may usually touch a carcass
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא asks whether ordinary Jews are forbidden to touch a נבלה. It answers that only the כהנים are warned against becoming טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way in a ברייתא: "And their carcass you shall not touch." One might think ordinary Jews are warned against touching a carcass. So the תורה says: "Speak to the כהנים, the sons of אהרן." The sons of אהרן are warned, but ordinary Jews are not warned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to support רבי יצחק. This first part shows that ordinary Jews are normally allowed to become טמא, which prepares for the conclusion in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If ordinary Jews may usually become טמא, the warning ״וּבְנִבְלָתָם לֹא תִגָּעוּ״ cannot be a year-round rule for them. So the פסוק needs a special time when it applies. That sets up the answer: the רגל.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא also teaches this, offered as support

phrases.english: This is also taught in a baraita:
"And their carcass you shall not touch."
One might think that ordinary Jews are warned
against touching a carcass;
therefore the verse says:
"Speak to the priests, the sons of Aharon,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 21:1. This פסוק goes on to forbid כהנים from becoming טמא to a dead person.

phrases.english: the sons of Aharon are warned,
the children of Israel are not warned.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא נָמֵי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to support רבי יצחק's teaching.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יצחק's rule that one must be טהור on the רגל
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that reads ״אֱמוֹר אֶל הַכֹּהֲנִים״ as limiting the ban on becoming טמא to כהנים

steps.title: A קל וחומר shows the same thing
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds a קל וחומר: if ordinary Jews may become טמא to a dead person, which is a severe טומאה, they may surely touch a נבלה, which is a lighter טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And isn't this a קל וחומר? If with severe טומאה the כהנים are warned but ordinary Jews are not, then with light טומאה, all the more so ordinary Jews are not warned.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא strengthens its point with simple logic. Ordinary Jews are clearly not forbidden to touch a נבלה during the year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even without a פסוק, logic shows that a light טומאה cannot be forbidden to people who are allowed to have a severe one. This makes the question even stronger: what is ״וּבְנִבְלָתָם לֹא תִגָּעוּ״ coming to teach?

keyTerms.meaning: An argument from a stricter case to a lighter one, or the reverse
Severe impurity, here from a dead person
Light impurity, here from an animal carcass

phrases.english: But is this not a kal vachomer?
If with severe impurity
phrases.notes: He means becoming טמא to a dead person.

phrases.english: priests are warned,
but ordinary Jews are not warned,
then with light impurity, is it not all the more so?

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲלֹא דְּבָרִים קַל וָחוֹמֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a logical argument to the ברייתא's point that ordinary Jews may become טמא.
steps.raayaObject: That ordinary Jews are normally allowed to touch a נבלה
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר from the severe טומאה of a dead person

steps.title: The verse must be talking about the Festival
steps.stepSummary: Since ordinary Jews may usually touch a נבלה, the פסוק ״וּבְנִבְלָתָם לֹא תִגָּעוּ״ must refer to the רגל, which supports רבי יצחק.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, why does the תורה say "And their carcass you shall not touch"? It is about the רגל.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא concludes that the warning against touching a נבלה applies on the רגל. This matches what רבי יצחק said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק cannot be a year-round ban for ordinary Jews, but the תורה does not write extra words. So it applies to a special time: the רגל, when everyone must be טהור to go up to the מקדש and eat קדשים.

keyTerms.meaning: Why then does the תורה say this?

steps.whatToRemember: The Torah's warning against touching a נבלה is read as applying to the רגל, so every Jew must be טהור for the רגל.

phrases.english: Rather, what does the verse teach by saying
"And their carcass you shall not touch"?
On the Festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, מָה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the result of steps 14 and 15 to give the פסוק its meaning.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: ״וּבְנִבְלָתָם לֹא תִגָּעוּ״ teaches that everyone must be טהור on the רגל, as רבי יצחק said.

steps.title: Three books are opened on ראש השנה
steps.stepSummary: רבי כרוספדאי in the name of רבי יוחנן teaches that three books are opened on ראש השנה. צדיקים גמורים are sealed for life right away, and רשעים גמורים are sealed for death right away. בינוניים wait until יום הכפורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי כרוספדאי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Three books are opened on ראש השנה: one of the completely wicked, one of the completely righteous, and one of those in the middle. The completely righteous are written and sealed right away for life. The completely wicked are written and sealed right away for death. Those in the middle stay undecided from ראש השנה until יום הכפורים. If they earn merit, they are written for life. If they do not, they are written for death.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the topic of judgment on ראש השנה. רבי יוחנן describes how different kinds of people are judged.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not everyone's judgment is finished on ראש השנה. The בינוניים have a waiting period until יום הכפורים, and what they do in those days decides their fate. This explains why the days between ראש השנה and יום הכפורים matter so much.
steps.whatToRemember: צדיקים and רשעים are sealed on ראש השנה, but בינוניים have until יום הכפורים, and their deeds in that time decide their fate.
steps.whyThisMatters: This teaching is the basis for treating the days from ראש השנה to יום הכפורים as a special time for תשובה and good deeds.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי כְּרוּסְפָּדַאי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Kruspedai said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
Three books are opened on Rosh Hashanah:
one of the completely wicked,
and one of the completely righteous,
and one of those in the middle.
The completely righteous are written and sealed
immediately for life;
the completely wicked are written and sealed
immediately for death;
those in the middle are left undecided
from Rosh Hashanah until Yom Kippur.
If they earn merit, they are written for life;
if they do not earn merit, they are written for death.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי כְּרוּסְפָּדַאי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of the רגל and returns to the theme of judgment on ראש השנה that ran through the opening steps (the שופר confusing the שטן, and being judged by one's present deeds).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On ראש השנה, צדיקים גמורים are sealed for life and רשעים גמורים for death. בינוניים are left undecided until יום הכפורים, and their merit decides their fate.

steps.title: A verse hinting at the three books
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבין finds the three books of step 17 in one פסוק from תהלים: the wicked, the righteous, and the in-between people.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבין said: Which פסוק teaches this? "Let them be blotted out of the book of the living, and let them not be written with the righteous." "Blotted out of the book" is the book of the totally wicked. "Of the living" is the book of the righteous. "And not be written with the righteous" is the book of the in-between people.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבין gives a פסוק as the source for רבי יוחנן's teaching that three books are opened on ראש השנה. He splits the פסוק into three parts, and each part matches one book.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each piece of the פסוק points to a different book. "Blotted out" fits the רשעים, who are erased from life. "The living" fits the צדיקים. The extra phrase "not written with the righteous" suggests a separate book for the בינוניים, who are written down but not together with the צדיקים.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the פסוק? (asking for the source)
Let them be blotted out, erased
In-between people, neither fully righteous nor fully wicked

phrases.english: Rabbi Avin said: What is the verse?
phrases.notes: Which פסוק hints at רבי יוחנן's three books from the last step?

phrases.english: "Let them be blotted out of the book of the living,
and with the righteous let them not be written."
phrases.notes: תהלים 69:29

phrases.aramaic: ״יִמָּחוּ מִסֵּפֶר״ — זֶה סִפְרָן שֶׁל רְשָׁעִים גְּמוּרִין,
phrases.english: "Let them be blotted out of the book": this is the book of the totally wicked;
"of the living": this is the book of the righteous;

phrases.aramaic: ״וְעִם צַדִּיקִים אַל יִכָּתֵבוּ״ — זֶה סִפְרָן שֶׁל בֵּינוֹנִיִּים.
phrases.english: "and with the righteous let them not be written": this is the book of the in-between people.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אָבִין, מַאי קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a פסוק as the source for the three books taught in step 17.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's teaching that three books are opened on ראש השנה

steps.title: A second verse for the three books
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק brings a different פסוק, משה's words in שמות, and reads three books out of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: We learn it from here: "And if not, please blot me out of Your book which You have written." "Please blot me out" is the book of the wicked. "Out of Your book" is the book of the righteous. "Which You have written" is the book of the in-between people.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק offers another פסוק as the source for the three books. It is a different source for the same idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He divides משה's request into three parts. "Blot me out" points to the רשעים. "Your book" points to the צדיקים, whose book is called God's own. "Which You have written" points to the third book, the one for the בינוניים. This does not argue with רבי אבין's idea. It is only a different פסוק for it.

phrases.aramaic: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר, מֵהָכָא:
phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said: From here:
"And if not, blot me out, please,
from Your book which You have written."
phrases.notes: שמות 32:32. These are משה's words to ה׳ after the sin of the golden calf.

phrases.english: "Blot me out, please": this is the book of the wicked;
"from Your book": this is the book of the righteous;
"which You have written": this is the book of the in-between people.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר, מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different פסוק for the same teaching that step 18 supported.
steps.raayaObject: The three books of judgment from step 17

steps.title: Three groups on the great Day of Judgment
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes בית שמאי: on the future יום הדין there are three groups. The צדיקים גמורים are sealed right away for eternal life, and the רשעים גמורים are sealed right away for גיהנם. A פסוק from דניאל supports this.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches that בית שמאי say: There are three groups on the Day of Judgment: the totally righteous, the totally wicked, and the in-between. The totally righteous are written and sealed immediately for eternal life. The totally wicked are written and sealed immediately for גיהנם. As the פסוק says: "Many of those who sleep in the dust of the earth will wake up, some to eternal life and some to shame and everlasting disgrace."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with a similar three-way split, but this time about the great judgment in the future. It first explains what happens to the fully righteous and the fully wicked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This matches רבי יוחנן's three types of people, but it is about a different judgment: the one after people "wake from the dust." The פסוק names only two outcomes, eternal life and disgrace. Those fit the two extreme groups, who are sealed right away. The middle group is dealt with next.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא

steps.confusionAlert: Here יום הדין is not ראש השנה. The פסוק talks about people waking up from the dust, so this is the great judgment of the future.

phrases.english: It was taught: Beit Shammai say:
There are three groups for the Day of Judgment:
one of the totally righteous,
and one of the totally wicked,
and one of the in-between people.
The totally righteous are written and sealed
immediately for eternal life;
the totally wicked are written and sealed
immediately for Gehenna,
as it says: "And many of those who sleep in the dust of the earth will wake,
these to eternal life,
and these to shame and everlasting disgrace."
phrases.notes: דניאל 12:2

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the yearly judgment on ראש השנה to a similar three-group split at the future יום הדין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On the future יום הדין, the צדיקים גמורים are sealed right away for eternal life, and the רשעים גמורים are sealed right away for גיהנם.

steps.title: The in-between people go down to גיהנם
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא begins to describe the third group: the בינוניים go down to גיהנם. The sentence continues in the next part of the גמרא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The in-between people go down to גיהנם...
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now turns to the middle group and says they go down to גיהנם. This is a setup line: the sentence is not finished, and the גמרא explains what happens to them next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the two extreme groups, the בינוניים are not sealed right away for a final outcome. Saying they "go down" hints that their story does not end there, and the next lines will explain it.

phrases.english: The in-between people go down to Gehenna,
phrases.notes: The sentence keeps going in the next lines of the גמרא, so hold on for the rest.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּינוֹנִיִּים יוֹרְדִין לְגֵיהִנָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא of בית שמאי with the third group.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The בינוניים go down to גיהנם. The details continue in the next section.
